claim_tested: Low GDP acts somewhere other than the catalytic site
key_finding: High GDP dephosphorylates phospho-p36 with coincident GTP formation (substrate behaviour); 100-fold lower GDP does not dephosphorylate yet stimulates phosphorylation; stimulation survives dilution; gel filtration shows an unaltered non-interacting alpha-beta dimer; GDP-beta-S distinguishes allosteric from catalytic site
organism_or_assay_context: Dictyostelium discoideum lysates and partially purified SCS
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Single laboratory; no Kd, Hill analysis or direct binding measurement for the stimulatory site; site not localised to a subunit

claim_tested: Micromolar GDP raises the rate of phosphoenzyme formation
key_finding: Stimulation from either GTP or succinyl-CoA plus Pi; apparent rate rises without significant change in the fraction of phosphorylated enzyme; effect retained through purification and seen with purified pig heart SCS
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. Rate-with-unchanged-endpoint is also the signature of a relieved rate-limiting step; 'allosteric' is an exclusion inference

claim_tested: The GDP effect requires a site on SCS itself
key_finding: GDP raising phosphoenzyme level is dependent on a protein distinct from SCS; effector separates by ammonium sulfate fractionation; reconstitution shows the protein inhibits SCS, GDP relieves the inhibition, and the inhibitor recognises both E. coli and eukaryotic SCS
organism_or_assay_context: E. coli SCS plus eukaryotic SCS, in vitro reconstitution
confidence_and_limitations: High for the existence of the trans-acting inhibitor. Same laboratory as the two papers above, published later; the effector protein is not identified

claim_tested: A second nucleotide site exists on SCS
key_finding: Depositors describe one nucleotide site only: 'GTP is bound in the ATP-grasp domain' of the beta subunit; Gln-20beta sets guanine specificity, Arg-54beta grips the gamma-phosphate. No second or regulatory site is claimed
confidence_and_limitations: High for what the authors assert. The deposited coordinates do contain a second GTP that the paper does not discuss

claim_tested: Any SCS structure has a nucleotide outside the beta catalytic site
key_finding: Census of 48 SCS-family entries from RCSB sequence search at 30% identity: 14 carry a nucleotide (1CQI ADP; 2FP4 GTP x2; 2FPG, 7JFP, 7JMK, 3UFX GDP; 7JJ0 GMPPCP; 7JKR GMPPNP; 6NO0-6NO5 ADP). Contact analysis at 4.0-4.2 A assigns every catalytic nucleotide exclusively to beta residues; alpha contributes zero residues in six of eight complexes and one of nineteen in 7JJ0 and 7JKR
organism_or_assay_context: Pig, E. coli, Thermus aquaticus, Blastocystis hominis
confidence_and_limitations: High. Limited to deposited structures; a transient or low-occupancy site would not appear

claim_tested: 2FP4 GTP 404 is a genuine second site
key_finding: GTP 404 contacts only beta Gly55, Lys56, Gly57, Lys64, Gly65, the same loop that grips the catalytic nucleotide (2.7 A away in 2FP4; 1.9-2.7 A in the five siblings). Mean 3.3 protein heavy atoms within 5 A per ligand atom, 10 of 32 atoms with none, versus 8.5 and 3 of 32 for catalytic GTP 403; B 41.8 vs 38.3 vs 29.3 for protein CA. Absent from 2FPG, 7JFP, 7JMK, 7JJ0, 7JKR across three space groups. Only alpha contact (Lys50 alpha) is a lattice neighbour after P 65 symmetry expansion. 2FP4 grown in 5 mM GTP; 2FPG grown in 5 mM GDP in the same crystal form shows no second copy
confidence_and_limitations: High. Occupancy was modelled at 1.00 by the depositors, but burial, B factors and non-reproducibility all indicate a high-concentration surface position

claim_tested: A guanine-nucleotide-sized pocket exists on alpha or at the alpha-beta interface
key_finding: Apo 4XX0 chain A (alpha): largest five cavities 31, 31, 24, 21, 21 A3. Positive control 2FP4 chain B catalytic pocket: 342 A3, centre 0.4 A from GTP 403. Interface cavities in the 4XX0 dimer: 630 A3 between the C-terminal domains, then 90, 81 (= site II, 0.3 A from the CoA thiol and 0.5 A from PO4) and 61 A3. A guanine nucleotide needs roughly 300 A3
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate-high. Grid method on static crystal structures; a cryptic pocket that opens on ligand binding would be missed

claim_tested: Any candidate site must be conserved between Dictyostelium and pig
key_finding: Alpha: Dicty P36967 vs pig 73.5% identity; beta: Dicty Q869S7 vs pig 59.7%. Second-site patch residues are conserved pig to Dicty (Gly55beta/Gly80, Lys56beta/Lys81, Gly57beta/Gly82, Lys64beta/Lys90, Gly65beta/Gly91) but degraded in E. coli (Gly57beta to Ala, nothing aligned to Lys64beta). Catalytic histidine pig His259alpha corresponds to Dicty scsA His268
confidence_and_limitations: High for the alignment. Conservation of the patch is expected because it is part of the catalytic nucleotide site, so it carries no information about a regulatory function

claim_tested: Depositors annotate a regulatory nucleotide site
key_finding: All 57 site records across the 14 nucleotide-containing entries carry EVIDENCE_CODE: SOFTWARE with template descriptions; the six 7J* entries have none. No depositor names a regulatory, allosteric or secondary site
confidence_and_limitations: High. Absence of depositor assertion, not evidence of absence of a site

claim_tested: Current annotation already asserts a nucleotide site on alpha
key_finding: P36967 carries no GO:0005525, GO:0019003 or GO:0032561 and no regulatory term; nucleotide and Mg binding sit on the beta subunits Q869S7 and Q55AI5, entirely on ECO:0000256 InterPro evidence. The two ECO:0000314 annotations on P36967 (GO:0004776, GO:0016020) both trace to PMID:8448193

claim_tested: A second lower-affinity nucleotide occupancy of the beta site could explain the effect
key_finding: Mn-ADP binds E at one or two sites with K2 = 0.5 microM; free ADP binds about 126-fold more weakly than Mn-ADP
confidence_and_limitations: Moderate. 'One or two sites' in an alpha2beta2 enzyme corresponds to the two catalytic sites; the pig enzyme where the effect is also seen is a single-catalytic-site alpha-beta dimer
